chunks: By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman called for his son at the time of his death, and he advised him, saying: O my son! Show indifference toward what is in the hands of people, for in that lies richness. Beware of seeking favors from people, for that is manifest poverty. Be better today than you were yesterday. When you pray, pray as one bidding farewell to this world, as though you will not return to it. And beware of that for which you must apologize.

key_terms.الغنى: Richness/sufficiency -- true wealth comes from not needing what people possess
key_terms.اليأس: Despair/indifference toward worldly possessions -- here meaning self-sufficiency and contentment by not coveting what others have
key_terms.فقر حاضر: Manifest poverty -- spiritual impoverishment from depending on others
key_terms.مودع: One bidding farewell -- praying with full awareness as if it is your last prayer

ai.seo_question: What was the deathbed advice of Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman to his son?
ai.summary: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, the renowned companion of the Prophet (SAWW) and keeper of his secrets, gave these counsels to his son on his deathbed. He urged self-sufficiency, continuous self-improvement, mindful prayer as if each prayer were the last, and avoidance of actions requiring apology -- principles widely taught in Islamic ethics as foundational to upright character.
